quick_skim.title: Decoding Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell RNA Velocity
quick_skim.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing provides snapshots of cellular states, while RNA velocity offers directional information about their temporal evolution. A fundamental question is whether hidden gene regulatory networks governing cellular dynamics can be recovered from such incomplete observations. In this work, we develop a mathematical framework for regulatory network reconstruction from RNA velocity data by formulating the problem as a sparse dynamical inverse problem arising from coupled transcription-splicing dynamics. We show that passive snapshot observations are generally insufficient to uniquely identify regulatory interactions, revealing an intrinsic limitation of unperturbed measurements. We then prove that controlled perturbations restore identifiability by generating informative regulatory trajectories and characterize conditions for unique recovery. To address noisy and imperfect observations, we introduce an integral reconstruction approach that avoids numerical differentiation and establish finite-sample guarantees for sparse network recovery. Our results provide a mathematical foundation for understanding when and how gene regulatory networks can be decoded from single-cell observations, linking perturbation design, inverse problem theory, and predictive modeling of cellular responses.

quick_skim.title: FlowGRN: Scalable and Dropout-Robust Gene Regulatory Network Inference via Flow Matching-Based Trajectory Reconstruction (Technical Report)
quick_skim.abstract: Inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data offers insights into cellular behavior, but is complicated by the lack of temporal information and the prevalence of dropout noise. To address these challenges, we present FlowGRN, a method that integrates conditional flow matching and score matching for robust trajectory reconstruction with dynGENIE3 for scalable GRN inference. FlowGRN incorporates a novel cell similarity measure that is resilient to dropout effects in high-dimensional scRNA-seq data. Evaluation on the BEELINE benchmark demonstrates that FlowGRN achieves state-of-the-art performance on both synthetic and experimental datasets. Ablation studies validate the importance of both the dropout-robust similarity measure and the trajectory reconstruction step, highlighting FlowGRN's ability to accurately model dynamic regulatory relationships.
